title: Quantum Error-Corrected Memories Keep Proper Time
authors: Sebastian P. Kish, Simon J. Devitt
abstract: What does quantum error correction do to relativistic proper time? We show that when two error-corrected quantum memories follow distinct worldlines and are controlled by local references, their local correction histories factor exactly from the proper-time difference between them. Error correction therefore does not erase time dilation: when the memories are compared, the accumulated difference appears as a relational phase rotation. During locally referenced operation this rotation is invisible to every local error syndrome; at discrete phases admitted by a code, the final relational evolution instead returns exactly as a deterministic logical gate, including an $S$-type Clifford gate at a $π/2$ excursion. These results connect fault-tolerant quantum information with relativistic clocks and establish protected quantum memories as a platform for preserving proper-time information and for long-coherence tests of quantum evolution involving relativistic proper time.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the interplay between quantum error correction and relativistic time dilation by examining how the relative phase accumulated between two separated quantum memories is preserved. The authors show that QEC does not eliminate the time difference, instead encoding it as a measurable relational phase rotation. This establishes protected quantum memories as a novel platform for testing quantum evolution involving relativistic time.
main_problem: The paper investigates how quantum error correction (QEC) affects the measurement of relativistic proper time differences ($\Delta	au$) between two quantum memories following distinct worldlines.
main_result: Error correction does not erase time dilation; the accumulated time difference manifests as a measurable relational phase rotation, which can be converted into a deterministic logical gate at specific time intervals.
method: The analysis uses theoretical derivations involving the evolution of joint quantum states under local operations, projecting the evolution onto the code space defined by stabilizer codes.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum memories whose local evolution is governed by a clock transition frequency ($\omega_0$). The comparison is modeled by analyzing the relative evolution operator $U_{	ext{rel}}$ between two memories separated in spacetime.
key_observables: Relative phase rotation ($\delta	heta$), code-space survival probability ($	ext{psurv}$), and conditional process fidelity ($	ext{Fcond}$).
important_parameters: The proper time difference ($\Delta	au$), the code structure (e.g., phase-flip code), and the amplification factor ($A$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the code satisfies its normaliser condition and treats the relative phase as a coherent systematic offset rather than a decay mechanism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate that locally corrected memories accumulate only the relative phase $\delta	heta(t) = \omega_0\Delta	au(t)$, and show code-space filtering for the phase-flip code at specific phase excursions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the relative phase accumulation (Theorem 1), then analyzing how QEC preserves this phase (Corollary 1), and finally detailing the conversion of this continuous phase into discrete logical gates (Corollary 2).
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, physical realization where fundamental concepts of general relativity (time dilation) are mapped onto the abstract framework of fault-tolerant quantum computation, suggesting protected quantum memories are viable for relativistic metrology.
